services.faq1A: A Clinic Website takes 3-4 weeks. A Clinic Growth System takes 6-8 weeks, depending on the number of treatments and languages.

services.faq2A: There are two fixed-price packages: the Clinic Website from {clinicPrice} and the Clinic Growth System from {growthPrice}, both in US dollars. I confirm a fixed quote for your scope before work starts, with no hourly billing.

services.faq7A: Yes. Cookie consent, handling of form data and a privacy policy are part of every clinic site.

services.faq9A: Yes. The code, content, domain and hosting accounts are in your clinic's name, and you get full access. No lock-in.

audit.eyebrow: Free for clinics with international patients
audit.heading: The 30-Day International Patient Website Playbook
audit.intro: What to fix on your clinic website, and in what order, so more of the patients who find you send an inquiry. Each chapter closes one gap, with the steps and the templates ready to paste.
audit.trust: No login. Your answers stay in your browser until you decide to send them.
benefits: Your score out of 100, and where you stand against clinics competing for the same patients
Your 3 fixes in order, each matched to the playbook chapter that closes it
A personal written audit of your actual site, done by me, within 48 hours

languages.q: Does your site have full pages in the languages your target patients speak?
languages.why: A patient in Riyadh or Lyon compares four or five clinics in one evening, in their own language. If yours is only in English or Turkish, they close the tab and message the next clinic, and the click you paid for is gone.
languages.fix: Build complete pages, not a translated home page, for your top 2 or 3 patient markets: every treatment, the doctors, the prices and the FAQ. Have them written by a native speaker (for Arabic that also means a proper right-to-left layout) and put the language switch where a phone user can see it.
languages.impact: Decides whether paid traffic from a market converts at all

journey.q: Does your site explain the whole trip: consultation, travel, stay, treatment and aftercare?
journey.why: A patient abroad rarely hesitates on the treatment. They hesitate on the logistics: who picks me up, where do I sleep, how many days, who do I call if something goes wrong once I am home. A site that leaves those open sends them to the clinic that answers.
journey.fix: Add one page that walks through the trip step by step: online consultation, flight and airport pickup, hotel, treatment days, follow-up after they fly home, and who they can message at each stage. Link it from every treatment page and use it to answer the questions you already hear on WhatsApp every week.
journey.impact: Turns interested readers into patients who are ready to book

whatsapp.q: Is there a WhatsApp button on every treatment page?
whatsapp.why: Most international patients write on WhatsApp, not through forms. If the button lives only on the contact page, the patient who was ready on the treatment page has to go looking, and many simply do not.
whatsapp.fix: Put a WhatsApp button on every treatment page, visible without scrolling on a phone, with a pre-filled message that names the treatment. Reply from a business account with a greeting in the patient's language, and set reply hours so nobody waits all night without an answer.
whatsapp.impact: Usually the single biggest lever for WhatsApp inquiries

speed.q: Does your site load in under 3 seconds on a phone with a normal mobile connection?
speed.why: Patients browse on phones, often on mobile data, often straight from an ad. A page that is still loading gets closed, and you have already paid for that click. Google also ranks slow pages lower, so you pay twice.
speed.fix: Compress every image to WebP and under 200 KB, remove the hero video and sliders, and cut unused scripts and chat widgets. Test the treatment pages, not the home page, on a real phone over 4G, and test again after every change.
speed.impact: Protects every other fix: nothing converts on a page nobody waits for

treatments.q: Does each treatment page show a price range and the recovery time?
treatments.why: Price and recovery time are the two questions every patient has before they write. Hiding them does not avoid the price talk, it moves it to a competitor who answers in the open. Pages that answer get more inquiries and better-qualified ones.
treatments.fix: Give each treatment its own page with a from-price, what is included (hotel, transfers, medication), how many days in Istanbul and when the patient can fly home. Add the 5 questions your coordinators answer most often, with honest answers.
treatments.impact: Raises both the number and the quality of inquiries

credentials.q: Are your doctors' credentials and the clinic's accreditations easy to find?
credentials.why: A patient flying to another country needs a reason to trust you before they write. Names, diplomas, memberships and certificates give it. Stock photos and 'expert team' do not, and the doubt stays until a competitor removes it.
credentials.fix: Add a page per doctor with a real photo, qualifications, years of practice and the number of procedures. Show accreditations and certificates where patients can check them, and link to the body that issued each one.
credentials.impact: Removes the doubt that stops a first message

gallery.q: Do you show before-and-after results with written patient consent?
gallery.why: Results are the strongest proof you have. Without them the patient compares you on price alone. Without consent you are one complaint away from taking the gallery down.
gallery.fix: Publish a before-and-after gallery grouped by treatment, with the same lighting and angles for every case, consent on file for each one and faces hidden where the patient asked. Add two lines per case: age range, what was done, how many days.
gallery.impact: Lets patients compare you on results instead of price

booking.q: Can a patient reach a consultation request in two taps or fewer from any page?
booking.why: Every extra step loses people. A patient who has to find the contact page, scroll and fill eight fields on a phone often stops halfway, and you never know they were there.
booking.fix: Add a sticky consultation button on mobile and a short form that asks only for name, contact and treatment. Let them attach a photo if they want to, and confirm on screen what happens next. Everything else can wait for the conversation.
booking.impact: Turns the visitors you already have into inquiries, without new traffic

tracking.q: Do you know which country and which source each inquiry came from?
tracking.why: Without it you cannot tell whether Germany or Saudi Arabia is working, or whether the budget should go to Google or Instagram. So you keep paying for the markets that do not book.
tracking.fix: Track WhatsApp clicks, form sends and calls as events, with the page and the language. Store every inquiry with its country, source and treatment in one place, a CRM or even a shared sheet, that your team updates when the patient books.
tracking.impact: The difference between guessing where patients come from and knowing

feedback.q: Are booked patients reported back to Google Ads or your CRM as conversions?
feedback.why: Google optimises for whatever you tell it. If it only sees clicks, it buys clicks. If it sees booked patients, it buys more of those, and the cost per patient comes down month after month.
feedback.fix: Pass each inquiry to your CRM with its click id, mark the ones that book, and upload those to Google Ads as offline conversions every week. Then set the campaigns to optimise for that conversion, not for clicks or form views.
feedback.impact: Lowers your cost per patient without raising the budget

maker.heading: Awab Elkhalil, web designer in Istanbul
maker.text: I design and build websites for clinics that treat international patients, made to turn visitors into inquiries and inquiries into booked patients. The playbook puts the same fixes I build into clinic sites in writing, so your team can make them too.

items.a: Yes. No payment, no card and no call. Enter your email and the playbook opens right away, with all 10 chapters, the 17 templates and the lead tracker.
It is used to send you your personal link to the playbook, so you can come back to it later. No newsletter, and your address is not shared with anyone.

items.q: How long does it take to apply?
items.a: Reading all 10 chapters takes about an hour. Each quick win takes under an hour, and the full plan is paced over 30 days so your team can work through it next to their usual work.

Not for most of it. The WhatsApp, pricing, patient trip, doctor and results chapters are changes your team can make on the site you have. Speed and tracking are easier with a developer, and every step is written so you can hand it over as it is.
